The silhouette width is 96 on every row, with no outline, no front face, no eave or edge line and no standing volume. The column scans show only a repeating dark base with isolated 1-row highlights, which are crack or seam marks rather than edge lines. It reads as a flat top-down ground surface, which is correct for a terrain tile.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dark purple cracked-stone ground. It shows 7 visible tones per 16x16 tile, matching the paving reference (7) and well above the grass reference (3). Near-flat coverage is 0%, the same as both references. Its dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the crack lines carry a purple tint rather than a black sticker outline. By eye I count about 4 dark purple body steps plus 2 violet highlight steps, so roughly 6 steps against the references' 5-6. Cracks, per-stone shading and highlight flecks give grain with no large flat areas. The weaker point is that the motif repeats identically across the patch, and the palette has only 7 colours in total. Even so, that density at tile level matches the paving reference, so a careful artist would accept it next to it without it looking thinner or flatter.
